display.title: Getting Ready for Pesach: Chametz, Matzah and Helping at Home
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains how we search for and sell our chametz before Pesach, why eating matzah on both Seder nights is a must, and how children can help prepare.
display.summary_long: A short pre-Pesach teaching from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast ten days before the holiday. Uncle Yossi explains that the house must be cleaned of all chametz (bread, cookies, cakes) before Pesach. On the night before Erev Pesach we search the whole house in bedikas chametz, making sure not a speck is left. Because the Torah forbids even owning chametz on Pesach, leftover chametz is locked away and sold to a non-Jew through a contract arranged by the local rav, who must be contacted in time. Eating matzah on the first two nights of Pesach is a must for every Jew, a mitzvah we wait for all year. Finally, children can earn Tzivos Hashem points by rolling up their sleeves to help Mommy and Tatty with the Pesach preparations, always with simchah, thanking Hashem for letting us celebrate Pesach once again.
display.lesson: Help get the house ready for Pesach, make sure to eat matzah on both Seder nights, and do it all with joy.

date.note: Says Erev Pesach is Friday 5 April and bedikas chametz 'next Thursday night, the 4th of April' (Pesach 5745); clip of episode 169.

quality.notes: Names the 1985 calendar dates (Erev Pesach Friday 5 April); otherwise timeless Pesach guidance.
